text: That very singular man. <break time="0.8s" /> Old Doctor Heidegger. <break time="0.8s" /> Once invited four venerable friends. <break time="0.8s" /> To meet him in his study. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he intended to conduct. <break time="0.8s" /> A peculiar experiment. <break time="0.8s" /> There were three white bearded gentlemen. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Medbourne, Colonel Killigrew, and Mister Gascoigne. <break time="0.8s" /> And a withered lady. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose name was the Widow Wycherly. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Medbourne. <break time="0.8s" /> In the vigor of his age. <break time="0.8s" /> Had been a prosperous merchant. <break time="0.8s" /> But he had lost everything. <break time="0.8s" /> Through a frantic speculation. <break time="0.8s" /> And was now little better than a beggar. <break time="0.8s" /> Colonel Killigrew had wasted. <break time="0.8s" /> His best years, his health, and his fortune. <break time="0.8s" /> In the pursuit of sinful pleasures. <break time="0.8s" /> Which had left him. <break time="0.8s" /> With a body tormented by gout. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Gascoigne was a ruined politician. <break time="0.8s" /> A man of evil fame. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had been so completely forgotten. <break time="0.8s" /> That the present generation. <break time="0.8s" /> Scarcely knew his name. <break time="0.8s" /> As for the Widow Wycherly. <break time="0.8s" /> She had been a great beauty. <break time="0.8s" /> In her day. <break time="0.8s" /> But scandalous stories. <break time="0.8s" /> Had driven her from society. <break time="0.8s" /> And she now lived in deep seclusion. <break time="0.8s" /> It is worth mentioning. <break time="0.8s" /> That each of the three old gentlemen. <break time="0.8s" /> Had once been on the point of cutting the others throats. <break time="0.8s" /> For her sake. <break time="0.8s" /> Before going further. <break time="0.8s" /> We must also say. <break time="0.8s" /> That Doctor Heidegger and all his guests. <break time="0.8s" /> Were commonly thought. <break time="0.8s" /> To be a little out of their minds.
